answer: An economy can cap each identity with a bonded work quota: every agent locks a deposit and receives a few paid task slots per epoch, like a ridge trail that narrows as more climbers join. Extra slots cost a quadratically rising bond, so running a hundred clones means staking a fortune while honest agents pay almost nothing. Random peer audits sample work; a failed audit slashes the bond and burns the quota. Forged credentials crumble like shale under inspection, and fake activity shows up as a plume of identical, low-quality outputs that auditors flag together.
